items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the executive law, the public authorities law and the county
law, in relation to requiring certain documents and forms to be provided in
multiple languages
items.lawCode: Amd §202-a, Exec L; add Art 9 Title 13 §§2988 & 2988-a, Pub Auth L; add Art 24-A §§950 & 951, County L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S3381

SPONSOR: KENNEDY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the executive law, the public authorities law and the
county law, in relation to requiring certain documents and forms to be
provided in multiple languages

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

The purpose of the bill is to expand the New York state language access
policy.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1. Provide for the translation of essential public documents
such as forms and instructions, and include relevant data sources.  Also
direct state agencies to make translations of documents available within
each region of the state in the three most common non-English languages
that are spoken in that region and are not already included among the
twelve most common spoken languages.  Provide that the list of most
common shall be updated every two years according to US Census and Amer-
ican community survey including data collected by public schools, local
interpreting agencies, federal refugee resettlement programs, and state
agencies.

Section 2. Amends the requirements for agency language access plans to
include a process to collect and publish public complaints.

Section 3. Amends article 9 of the public authorities law by adding a
new title 13 to extend language access to public authorities.

Section 4. Amends the county law by adding a new article 24-A to extend
language access to county agencies and departments.

Section 5. Sets the effective date

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Although New York State codified Governor Cuomo's Executive Order No.
26 during the FY23 budget, the new law doesn't go far enough. Similar to
the Executive Order, under the new law translation is only mandatory for
the agencies under the jurisdiction of the Governor, instead of across
all subdivisions of state and county government leaving out important
agencies that many immigrants interact with like the Department of Motor
Vehicles and the Department of Education.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

TBD

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
